Compañía General de Combustibles (CGC).desc: An Argentine oil and gas producer that also holds stakes in gas pipeline companies (TGN, GasAndes and TGM). It is owned by the Eurnekian family through Corporación América, with Sociedad Comercial del Plata holding 30%; output reached a record 37,000 barrels of oil equivalent a day at the end of 2019.

Cyprus Popular Bank (Laiki).desc: A Cypriot bank, also known as Laiki Bank, with branches in Cyprus and Greece and subsidiaries and branches abroad. It was broken up under resolution in March 2013: its Greek branches went to Piraeus Bank and its Cypriot business, including insured deposits up to 100,000 euros, was transferred to Bank of Cyprus with effect from 26 March 2013, leaving a residual 'bad' bank.

Daewoo Engineering and Construction.desc: A South Korean general construction company founded in 1973, working in civil engineering, plants, buildings, housing and development. Jungheung Group companies completed the purchase of a 50.75% stake from Korea Development Bank in December 2021 for 2.1 trillion won (about US$1.8 billion).

De Beers.desc: A diamond company that explores for, mines, sorts and trades diamonds, develops consumer brands and makes synthetic diamonds for industrial use. Anglo American plc holds 85% and the Government of Botswana 15%.

sources.title: About Us

Dow Chemical.desc: The Dow Chemical Company is a chemicals maker whose products include polyethylene and other ethylene derivatives, polyurethanes, construction chemicals, coatings materials and silicones. It was incorporated in Delaware in 1947, succeeding a Michigan company of the same name organised in 1897, and is a wholly owned subsidiary of the New York-listed holding company Dow Inc., which reported sales of about $40 billion and roughly 34,600 full-time employees at 31 December 2025.

Dongfang Electric Corporation.desc: A Chinese maker of power generation equipment — wind, solar, hydro, nuclear, gas and thermal — plus chemical containers, environmental and hydrogen equipment and engineering contracting. It has state-owned capital in its paid-in capital, and its H shares are listed on the Hong Kong stock exchange alongside A shares; revenue was RMB 38.15 billion in the six months to 30 June 2025, with 18,511 employees at that date.

sources.title: 2025 Interim Report

Dundee Precious Metals.desc: A Canadian-based international gold mining company that acquires, explores, develops, mines and processes precious metals, with operations in Bulgaria, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Serbia and Ecuador. It is listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange and was renamed DPM Metals Inc. in September 2025 after buying Adriatic Metals.

EVN Group.desc: An Austrian energy and utility group, headquartered in Lower Austria, that supplies electricity, gas, heat, drinking water and wastewater services and runs waste-to-energy, internet and telecom businesses. Its shares are listed on the Vienna Stock Exchange; group revenue was 3,000.0 million euros in the 2024/25 financial year, with 7,997 staff at 30 September 2025, and it was active in 12 countries including Bulgaria and North Macedonia.

East African Crude Oil Pipeline (EACOP).desc: EACOP Ltd is the company building and operating the 1,447 km East African Crude Oil Pipeline from Kabaale in Uganda's Hoima district to the Chongoleani Peninsula near Tanga port in Tanzania, a roughly $4 billion investment. Its shareholders are TotalEnergies, Uganda National Oil Company, Tanzania Petroleum Development Corporation and CNOOC; the company does not publish their percentages on this page, and it has offices in Kampala, Dar es Salaam and London.

sources.title: About Us

Ecopetrol.desc: Colombia's integrated oil and gas company, incorporated in Colombia and based in Bogotá, which the company calls the largest company in Colombia; through its subsidiary ISA it also runs electricity transmission and toll roads. The Nation owns 88.49% of its voting capital; its shares have traded on the Colombian Stock Exchange since August 2007 and its American Depositary Shares on the New York Stock Exchange since September 2008. Group oil and gas production was 736,600 barrels of oil equivalent a day in 2023.

sources.title: Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2023

Eiffage.desc: A construction and concessions group that calls itself one of the leading European construction and concessions companies and says it is deeply rooted in France, with eight business lines covering construction, property, development, roads, civil engineering, metal, energy systems and concessions. Elecnor.desc: A Spanish group that develops, builds and operates infrastructure, energy and services projects, covering electricity, power generation, telecommunications, railways, construction, water and the environment. It also holds 51% of Celeo, which has transmission lines in Chile, Brazil and Peru; group sales were 3,810.1 million euros in 2024.

Enagás.desc: A Spanish gas infrastructure company that is technical manager of Spain's gas system and has been certified by the European Commission as an independent transmission system operator since August 2012. Vista Gold describes itself as engaged, directly and through joint ventures, in the exploration for and the acquisition, development and operation of mineral properties in North and South America; it was continued under the laws of the Yukon Territory, listed on the American and Toronto stock exchanges, and in February 2000 sold Yamin, the company owning the Capa Circa mine, to a miners' co-operative.

Daewoo Motor Co..desc: A South Korean carmaker whose reorganisation plan was approved by the Incheon court on 30 September 2002; on 17 October 2002 most of its assets — three plants and nine overseas subsidiaries — were transferred to a new company, GM Daewoo Auto & Technology, in which, on completion of the final equity injection, General Motors held 42.1%, creditors 33%, Suzuki 14.9% and SAIC 10%. Its Bupyeong plant was separated into Daewoo Incheon Motor Company, and remaining facilities, debts and liabilities stayed with Daewoo Motor's creditors.

Doe Run Peru.desc: Doe Run Peru S.R.L. is a Peruvian metals company that operated the La Oroya polymetallic smelter and refinery, bought from a Centromin subsidiary on 23 October 1997, and the Cobriza copper mine and mill, bought in August 1998. Doe Run Cayman Ltd. held more than 99% of it, with the rest held by employees as Peruvian law required; the whole chain was indirectly owned by The Renco Group, Inc. Its La Oroya division reported net sales of $435.5 million in fiscal 2003 (excluding sales to Doe Run) and, at 31 October 2003, 841 salaried and 2,296 hourly employees plus 957 contractors.

DynCorp.desc: A private, employee-owned US defence and government services company based in Reston, Virginia, whose main business was logistics support for the Department of Defense alongside state and local government services and information technology. At 31 December 2024 its shareholders were Genera Avante, S.L. (Inveravante) with 58.53%, Aurel, S.A. (Grupo Eleta) with 31.52% and COFIDES with FIEX holding 9.95%.
